cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: BACKWARD INTEGRATION - proprietary 'Fabric-to-Fibre' recycling. The Company imports end-of-life para-aramid fabrics (e.g. expired bulletproof vests) and processes them through a dedicated regenerating machine for high-strength fibres, converting them into secondary raw material used in brake pads, clutch facings, filtration media and protective textiles. Para Aramid Fabric Waste purchases were Rs 1,409.18 / 1,429.71 / 2,509.24 lakhs against total purchases of Rs 6,568.07 / 7,295.41 / 7,227.68 lakhs in FY26 / FY25 / FY24, being 21.46% / 19.60% / 34.72% of total purchase (the RHP's own computed line). The RHP states this reduces dependence on imported virgin fibres and lowers raw material costs. CAPTIVE ENERGY INTEGRATION - a 380 KW rooftop solar system at the Petlad unit (MGVCL connection released January 19, 2022) plus a ground-mounted solar plant on leased land at Kankanpur described as 4 MW (Our Business) / 5 MW DC and 4 MW AC (History chapter), commissioned per GETCO certificate of February 07, 2025 and GEDA certificate of April 30, 2025, which the RHP states 'has substituted a significant portion of our electricity requirements from Financial Year 2025-26 onwards'. FORWARD INTEGRATION (PROPOSED, NOT YET REVENUE-GENERATING) - the Company proposes to move downstream from modacrylic-based yarn into the manufacture and sale of modacrylic-based fabrics; this is being trialled through job work with third-party weaving units and third-party process houses, i.e. asset-light and NOT in-house weaving, with captive consumption of its own modacrylic yarn. NOT INTEGRATED / EXPOSED - the Company has no long-term or exclusive supply agreements with any supplier and no long-term purchase commitments with most customers; purchases are made on purchase orders that may be discontinued, modified or cancelled without significant prior notice. A large proportion of specialty fibres (para-aramid, meta-aramid, modacrylic, FR viscose) is imported: imports were 36.29% / 36.92% / 41.18% of total purchase in FY26 / FY25 / FY24 versus domestic 63.71% / 63.08% / 58.82%. Raw material and traded goods purchases were 68.51% / 70.23% / 72.20% of total expenses. Sourcing locations named: Gujarat, Maharashtra, China, USA, Thailand and Brazil. The Company avails duty-free imports under the Advance Authorisation Scheme and imports capital goods under the EPCG Scheme, both carrying export obligations. The Company holds no collaboration or performance-guarantee/marketing-assistance arrangement with any company, and has no holding company, subsidiary or joint venture. Distribution is direct B2B to industrial manufacturers, processors and institutional buyers, supported by participation in Messe Frankfurt exhibitions in Germany, Mumbai and Russia; there is no distributor or dealer network disclosed. Defect and rejection rates were 0.13% / 0.40% / 0.03% of revenue from operations in FY26 / FY25 / FY24. Average relationship length: approximately 6 years with major customers and approximately 5.5 years with major suppliers.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- All manufacturing is carried out at one facility at Petlad, Gujarat, and the Company operates in a single business segment — spinning of technical textile yarn. Any disruption, slowdown or shutdown at Petlad, or adverse developments in that one segment, hits the entire business with no alternative site or offsetting vertical.
- Top 1 / 3 / 5 / 10 customers contributed 19.75% / 39.77% / 51.57% / 67.40% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2025 (25.53% / 47.85% / 57.91% / 72.11% in Fiscal 2024). Loss of one large customer, a decline in its financial health or reduced demand would materially affect revenue and cash flow. China alone accounted for 19.75% of Fiscal 2025 revenue, matching the top-1 customer figure.
- There are no long-term agreements for supply of raw materials, and the majority is sourced from the top 10 suppliers (70.31% of purchases in Fiscal 2025). Para-aramid, viscose and acrylic fibres come from a limited number of customer-approved suppliers, so substitution is slow and disruption or price escalation passes into production schedules, volumes and margins.
- The business is heavily dependent on para-aramid based spun yarn and 100% polypropylene spun yarn, disclosed at 23.87% and 22.64% of revenue from operations respectively in Fiscal 2025 (32.10% and 21.27% in Fiscal 2024). Any fall in demand, inability to produce, or adverse price movement in these two yarns disproportionately affects results.
- The registered office, the Petlad manufacturing unit, the rooftop solar facility and the 4 MW ground-mounted solar project are all on leased property, and the Issue proceeds will install machinery on a leased factory. Early termination, non-renewal, or renewal on worse terms would jeopardise both operations and the return on Issue-funded capex.
- Exports were 38.05% of Fiscal 2025 revenue from operations and the Company carries an obligation to export against import of ₹ 535.82 lakhs as at March 31, 2025 (₹ 343.53 lakhs in Fiscal 2024). Failure to meet export obligations, or adverse changes in foreign trade policy or tariffs, would trigger duty liabilities and hurt cash flows.
- Debt-equity ratio rose to 1.60x in Fiscal 2025 from 1.27x, long-term borrowings grew 120.11% to ₹ 3,090.25 lakhs and short-term borrowings included director loans of ₹ 1,289.30 lakhs; short loans received from related parties were ₹ 1,778.63 lakhs in Fiscal 2025. The Company has also experienced negative cash flows in the recent past. ₹ 2,500.00 lakhs of Net Proceeds is earmarked to repay borrowings, so post-Issue re-leveraging is the item to watch.
- The proposed expansion depends on purchasing and installing new equipment and machinery for ₹ 2,495.75 lakhs against quotations, not firm orders, deployed across Fiscals 2026 and 2027. If investment in manufacturing technology falls short, or the added capacity is not absorbed at the assumed demand (an estimated 120 MT against present 55 MT capability), competitiveness and returns suffer.

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Deploy ₹ 2,495.75 lakhs of Net Proceeds towards new equipment and machinery at the existing Petlad manufacturing facility, split ₹ 1,247.87 lakhs in Fiscal 2026 and ₹ 1,247.88 lakhs in Fiscal 2027.**
- **Repay or pre-pay, in full or in part, ₹ 2,500.00 lakhs of certain borrowings availed by the Company, entirely from Net Proceeds in Fiscal 2026.**
- **General corporate purposes will be capped at the lower of 15% of gross proceeds or ₹ 1,000.00 lakhs.**
- **Scale up production capacity by expanding operations within the existing Petlad facility, deploying additional compact spinning systems and high-value yarn attachments such as the Pinter Hard Core system for core-spun and specialty yarns.**
- **Expand manufacturing to close the stated gap between an estimated demand of 120 MT and current manufacturing ability of 55 MT, which meets approximately 44% of demand.**
- **Expand global market reach and gradually grow the proportion of revenue generated from exports by adding capacity and targeting additional export markets for specialised technical yarns.**
- **Diversify the product portfolio by entering high-value technical yarn markets such as milled acrylic and milled carbon yarns for fire-resistant fabrics, composite reinforcement and advanced industrial textiles.**
- **Enhance capacity and capabilities in the Indutech and Protech segments, where demand for high-performance and application-specific textile materials is growing across chemicals, pharmaceuticals, safety equipment manufacturing and …**
- **Expand adoption of automation and digital tools across manufacturing and administrative processes, including integrated planning systems, automated inventory management and data-driven monitoring and analytics.**
- **The commissioned 4 MW captive solar power plant is expected to substitute a significant portion of the Company's electricity requirements from Financial Year 2025-26 onwards, contributing to cost savings.**
- **Outstanding obligation to export against import under duty exemption schemes stood at ₹ 535.82 lakhs as at March 31, 2025, up from ₹ 343.53 lakhs a year earlier; non-compliance would trigger duty liabilities.**
- **The Company, in consultation with the BRLM, may undertake a Pre-IPO Placement not exceeding 20% of the size of the Issue, with any amount so raised reduced from the Issue.**
